name: Unfurl — link preview inspector
title: Link preview inspector
summary: Paste any URL and the server fetches it, parses its OpenGraph and Twitter-card metadata, and renders the social preview card — a Next.js Route Handler plus an SSR page running on the Spacefast Functions runtime.
setup_questions: What should the tool be called (the name in the header and browser tab)?
What's the accent color (a hex like #b6ff3d), and should it feel like a dark developer tool or a light consumer app?
Which three example URLs should the landing page offer as one-click demos?
Should the result page expose the raw JSON from the API alongside the rendered card?
sections: Static landing page: hero, paste-a-URL form that GETs the SSR route, and one-click example links
SSR result page at /u?url=… that server-renders the preview card per request
Preview card: og:image with a graceful fallback, favicon, domain, title, description, site name, and canonical link
Route Handler at /api/unfurl?url=… returning normalized JSON, with SSRF hardening (scheme allowlist, private-address blocking, redirect cap, size cap, timeout)
Distinct error states for a malformed URL, a blocked address, a timeout, an upstream failure, and a page with no metadata
middleware.ts that normalizes a bare-domain url param and stamps security headers
based_on: The link-unfurling service every chat app runs behind the scenes — Slack, Discord, and iMessage all fetch a pasted URL server-side and render its OpenGraph card.
why_good: The canonical proof that Spacefast runs a real server. Cross-origin fetching and HTML parsing genuinely cannot happen in the browser, so this recipe cannot be faked with a static site: it exercises a Next.js Route Handler, per-request SSR, and middleware on the Functions runtime in one small app.
notes: Functions runtime project, not a prebuilt static output directory. Build and publish from site/ with the sf CLI: `sf publish` auto-detects the Next.js app and builds it with a pinned OpenNext Cloudflare adapter. Do not add `output: "export"` to next.config.ts and do not declare `export const runtime = "edge"` anywhere; both break the OpenNext build.
